subject: Re: Proposal: multi-year reserved capacity + annual prepay - ramp structure discussion
messages:
From: Kimberly Park <kimberly@redwood.ai>

Date: Mon, 14 Jul 2025 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Proposal: multi-year reserved capacity + annual prepay - ramp structure discussion

Hi Alyssa —

Thanks again for the thoughtful call this morning. Per our conversation I attached a draft ramp proposal that maps a 3-year reserved commitment into a phased GPU/TPM onramp that aligns with your product release milestones. Key highlights in the attached PDF:

- Year 1: lower base reserved pool (30% of peak) + option to burst to 60% (prepaid annual installment)
- Year 2: 60% committed baseline, earlier discount tier unlocked at 9 months subject to usage thresholds
- Year 3: full steady-state 100% committed baseline with highest term discount

We modeled two commercial levers: (A) annual prepay vs. upfront 3-year prepay; (B) a carryforward credit if Year N usage < committed units. The goal is to balance Peregrine's cash/ops predictability with Redwood's capacity planning.

Questions for your team:
1) Would you prefer a frontloaded Year 1 (higher prepay) to secure deeper Year 1 discounts, or do you need the lighter entry with graduated increases?
2) Is the primary constraint cashflow (procurement timing) or flexibility for product experiments (ability to ramp up/down early)?

I've looped in Rishi for pricing flex and Grace for success plan alignment on milestones. If you prefer, we can sketch an alternate front-loaded schedule with explicit refund/true-up mechanics.

Attached: Peregrine_Ramp_Proposal_v3.pdf (ramp diagram + numbers)

Next steps: if you can send procurement's timing for PO/annual invoice cadence, we'll produce a term sheet tailored to that cadence.

Best,
Kimberly Park
Enterprise Sales, Redwood Inference
kimberly@redwood.ai
[Attachment: Peregrine_Ramp_Proposal_v3.pdf]

Kimberly —

Appreciate the deck. High level: procurement is OK with committing for 3 years, but cashflow in FY26 is tight. Two specific asks from our side:

1) Can Redwood provide a stronger discount in Year 1 if we frontload a larger annual prepay (we'd be willing to move more spend into Yr1 if the delta is meaningful)
2) We need a clearly defined true-up and carryforward window (we prefer no expiration for credits within the contract term, but understand that impacts your capacity planning)

Also — our infra team flagged that the TPM footprint could be larger in Q4 of Year 1 depending on feature uptake; if we commit to frontloading, we want a defined bursting SLA (max burst capacity and notification window).

Procurement asks: please send a term sheet with milestone-linked deliverables and invoice schedule so finance can model.

Thanks —
Alyssa
Head of Product Partnerships, Peregrine AI
alyssa.chen@peregrine.ai

Subject: Re: Proposal: multi-year reserved capacity + annual prepay - ramp structure discussion

Alyssa / Kimberly —

Thanks for the clarity. A couple of constructs we've used successfully that might fit Peregrine's concerns:

- Frontloaded annual prepay with a stepped discount: e.g., 18% off list in Yr1 (if you prepay >= 65% of Yr3 target), 22% Yr2, 28% Yr3; includes a 12-month carryforward window for unused credits (not indefinite)
- Early-adopter burst pool: guaranteed burst of +30% for up to 90 days with a 7-day notice; additional burst available at on-demand rates if needed
- Milestone credits: if Redwood misses the targeted availability milestones tied to your Q4 ramp, we provide incremental credits toward next invoice (capped)

We can soften the carryforward to 18 months for your early years if that helps cashflow modeling. If procurement needs no-expiry credits, we can include a smaller upfront discount and maintain an unlimited credit carryforward, but that materially changes unit economics.

Kimberly — can you draft a term sheet with the frontloading option and a conservative carryforward (18 months) and annotate the commercial impact? Grace, please confirm the onboarding milestones and acceptance criteria so we can tie invoice triggers.

-Rishi
VP Sales, Redwood Inference

Kimberly / Rishi —

Finance here. A few procurement/legal items we need addressed in the draft term sheet before routing to controls:

- Invoice cadence: can Redwood accept annual invoices split into two equal installments per year (invoice in Jan and Jul)?
- SOC 2 clause: we require evidence of SOC 2 Type II within 30 days of contract signature or a committed remediation plan with milestones
- Termination / refund mechanics: please outline how prepaids are returned or credited in case of early termination; we prefer a pro-rata refund less a 6-month minimum usage fee

If you can provide a revised term sheet addressing the three bullets above (and include the frontloaded discount scenario), we can escalate. Also include an explicit contact for accounts payable to set up PO wiring instructions.

Thanks —
Peregrine Procurement

Team —

Attached is an updated term sheet (redwood-term-sheet-2025-07-15.docx) that addresses the procurement asks:

- Invoice cadence: annual invoice is split into Jan/Jul installments; we can also support a single upfront invoice if you prefer
- SOC 2: attached evidence link and a 30-day remediation plan outline; legal will add a SOC-commitment exhibit to the MSA
- Termination/refund: proposed pro-rata refund less a 6-month minimum usage fee; carryforward credits valid for 18 months by default, option to extend to unlimited carryforward in exchange for a 4% lower Yr1 discount

Commercial change in the frontloaded scenario (65% Yr1 prepay): Yr1 effective discount moves from 12% (baseline) to 20% — we call this the Frontload-65 option in the term sheet. I've added burst SLA language: +30% burst for 90 days with 7-day notice, additional burst at on-demand pricing.

Next steps: if procurement is comfortable with the Jan/Jul invoice cadence and the 18-month carryforward, we can send the DocuSign link for signature and lock the pricing. Legal is on cc to finalize the SOC exhibit.
